docs/lean-provenance.md's pin block and per-claim tables are GENERATED from this file:
python3 scripts/lean_provenance.py render   (rewrite the generated blocks)
python3 scripts/lean_provenance.py check    (fail if the doc drifted — runs in doc_lint)
python3 scripts/lean_provenance.py resolve  (Gate A: every symbol resolves, with its kind)
Prose cites claim_id and nothing else. Nobody hand-edits a citation string here or there.
'kind' is the Lean declaration keyword; 'shape' records the claim shape actually relied on,
because theorem/lemma are interchangeable and a def can be propositional (Kernel.HasBond is).

tables.title: The kernel and the three generated views
tables.stated_in: [`theory-fidelity.md`](theory-fidelity.md) ("What the kernel actually is"), [`spec/LENS_ENTRY_SPEC.md`](../spec/LENS_ENTRY_SPEC.md) §A/§C, `README.md`, `crates/bert-core/src/transition.rs` header table.

claims.claim: The kernel is Klir's `(T, R)` plus on-ness — the K ≅ **2** arrow
claims.gives: A definition, not a theorem: `dep_on` is the field forcing every dependency endpoint to be a thing. This is the structure everything below is generated from.

claims.claim: The Klir view is free, and it round-trips
claims.gives: Generation with no hypothesis (the maps are `def`s), and both round-trip identities as proved equalities (`rfl`).

claims.shape: a `Prop`-valued `def` used as a hypothesis — `toBunge (k) (hb : k.HasBond)`. Rust's `check_bond` is **strictly stronger than this definition, and the gap is unproved**: `HasBond` quantifies over relata with no type restriction (the kernel has no composition/environment split), while `check_bond` additionally requires both endpoints to be `System | Subsystem`. Two corpus entries turn on the difference — under the Lean, `mobus/steel-plant.sl` generates a Bunge view; under the Rust it is refused as an aggregate (#216). The theorems that make the generated view faithful are the separate rows below.
claims.gives: A kernel whose dependency contains a bonded pair of *distinct* relata generates a Bunge CES view (Def 1.1: unbonded collection = aggregate).
Projecting the generated view back fixes the kernel; distinct kernels generate distinct views; the generated system is closed.

claims.shape: as above — a `Prop`-valued `def` consumed as a hypothesis, `toMobus (k) (hi : k.Irreflexive)`. `check_self_loops` mirrors the **definition**.
claims.gives: A kernel with no self-dependency (§4.3, k ≠ o) generates a Mobus view via its flow network.
The generated view's total relation is exactly `dep`; projection fixes the kernel; distinct kernels generate distinct views.

claims.shape: a proved implication under **three** hypotheses — `HasBond`, `Irreflexive`, and `DepActs`. Drop any one and the triangle is not claimed; this is where a hostile reader pushes, so the hypotheses are named here rather than summarized as "both preconditions".
claims.gives: When all three hold, generating Mobus then projecting to Bunge equals generating Bunge directly — the commuting triangle with the kernel at the apex.

claims.claim: `HasBond` and `Irreflexive` are independent — parallel lenses, no tower
claims.shape: **a negative claim, checked by exhibition, not by a theorem.** No entailment theorem exists in either direction, by design; nothing here is proven, and this row must never be cited as proof of independence.
claims.gives: `fixtures/gates_truth_table.json` (this repo) contains rows passing each gate while failing the other — `n=2, dep=[[0,1],[1,1]]` bonded-but-reflexive; `n=1, dep=[]` irreflexive-but-unbonded — and those rows report the real predicates via the `_iff` bridges in `gates.iff-bridges`.

claims.claim: The fixture's gate booleans report the real ViewGeneration predicates, not look-alikes
claims.shape: two proved bi-implications. `hasBondB_iff` holds **under the total `ActsOn` instance** (the pinning of spec §C) — it is not instance-independent, and citing it without that hypothesis overstates it.
claims.gives: `hasBondB D = true ↔ (kernelOf D).HasBond` and `irreflexiveB D = true ↔ (kernelOf D).Irreflexive`.

claims.claim: Fixture and oracle evaluate the SAME declarations
claims.gives: One definition site for the boolean gates and the mode-verdict map both emitters import, so fixture and oracle cannot disagree with each other. Definitions, not theorems — the agreement is structural, not proved.

claims.claim: The fixture is Lean-emitted, not hand-written
claims.gives: The enumerator over every `(T, R)` kernel on `Fin n`, `n ≤ 2` (19 rows) that prints `fixtures/gates_truth_table.json` verbatim. (`main` sits outside the namespace, as an executable entry point.)

claims.claim: The subprocess oracle exists and speaks the documented contract
claims.gives: `lake exe gates-oracle` evaluates `hasBondB` / `irreflexiveB` on arbitrary stdin models — the unbounded cross-check above the fixture's 19 rows. A build target and a prose contract at the head of `GatesOracle.lean`, not a theorem.

tables.title: Bond semantics and the Mobus tuple
tables.stated_in: [`theory-fidelity.md`](theory-fidelity.md) (Bunge and Mobus sections), `crates/bert-canvas/src/lenses.rs` (bond criterion), this repo's `CLAUDE.md` §"Semantic authority". Tuple slot attribution is the terminology concordance's job ([`language/terminology-concordance.md`](language/terminology-concordance.md), row 1); this table maps only claim → proof.

claims.claim: "A flow that modifies history is a bond" — the bond criterion the kernel validates against
claims.gives: The predicate connecting a flow network to action pairs — the semantic side `check_bond`'s syntactic test is pinned to. A definition; nothing here proves that an author's `is_bond` declaration is *true* of the modeled world.
The action typeclass and the bonded-pair predicate `HasBond` quantifies over.

claims.claim: The tuple is a structure with E first-class, components and environment disjoint
claims.shape: a `structure` whose coherence constraints are **fields**, discharged at construction — not standalone theorems. The named fields are the ones this repo relies on; **the list is not an enumeration of the tuple's constraints**, which is why the post-pin sixth constraint (`interfaces_carry_flow`) leaves every claim here intact.
claims.gives: The machine-checked tuple (concordance row 1: E first-class is a Lean improvement over the printed 7-tuple); environment is a field, not an afterthought, and cannot overlap components.

claims.claim: Boundary completeness and the total relation
claims.gives: Every external flow crosses the boundary at an interface (**derived** from the bipartite field, not assumed); the system's total relation stays on its own furniture; internal edges connect components only.

tables.title: The decomposition seam (bert-lenses#89)
tables.stated_in: `crates/bert-core/src/decomposition.rs` (header transcription table — the Rust check is a literal transcription, row by row), [`design/decomposition-foundations.md`](design/decomposition-foundations.md).

claims.claim: The boundary contract is the eight fields of a structure, not prose
claims.shape: the count *eight* is a closed enumeration of this structure's constraint fields, and Gate A holds it closed: adding a ninth field upstream does not fail resolution, so **this row's count is re-checked by hand at each replay** (the one number the gate cannot defend).
claims.gives: Child sources/sinks biject with the component's inflows/outflows, kind-preserving, landing on interfaces, with `E′` derived as the parent's interior neighborhood — the contract `check_decomposition` transcribes.
The combined source+sink correspondence is a bijection; every parent boundary flow continues into the child with its substance kind intact.

claims.claim: Substitution is sound; depth-1 assembly is well-formed
claims.gives: Replacing the component by its child preserves the contract's guarantees; the depth-1 assembly of a decomposed model is itself a well-formed tuple.
